Quest-blocking memory leak in early reta.note: A memory defect of the early retail releases, fixed during the patch cycle before 483.07. It does not concern the 483.07 code the restoration follows.

Save corruption caused by the same early.note: Save corruption caused by the same early memory defect, fixed before 483.07. Kept separate from the save rollback reported for 483.07 (RPT-SAVE-0001).

Broad 483.04/05/051 machine-compatibilit.note: Machine-compatibility failures of 483.04 to 483.051, addressed mainly by 483.06. A historical and hardware matter, not 483.07 game logic.

Earlier save/load unreliability.note: General save/load unreliability of the earlier releases, improved by 483.07. The specific rollback that survives in 483.07 is tracked separately (RPT-SAVE-0001).

Graz exit/progression-state problem.note: The Graz exit/progression problem was fixed in 483.07; a save made with an earlier release can still carry the bad state, which is data in that file rather than 483.07 code.

Roland music plus DMA digital-audio regr.note: A sound-driver regression (Roland music with DMA digital audio) shipped with 483.07 and fixed by the separate March 1993 DRKSND driver update. A driver/hardware matter, not game logic.

High-reputation merchant buy/resell arbi.note: In 483.07 standing and fame cannot make an arbitrage: the buy price's standing term only ever surcharges, and the sell price's standing term and both fame terms truncate to 0 (Trading.cs, buy price R032+0x192E, sell price R032+0x1B26; noted in the OriginalBehaviour remarks). The exploit recalled from an earlier release is not in 483.07.

RPT-SAVE-0001.note: The save routine (R037+0x2ACE) writes the party, the events and the 414 location records from memory; in a battle it first reads locs.tmp and events.tmp back. Which transient state the official report means, and when a save would capture an earlier one, is not visible from the code alone.

RPT-PALETTE-0001.note: The figure colours are kept per party slot (R136+0x33FC, 5 x 24 bytes) and saved with the game. That table lies directly after the battle floor image (R136+0x0000, 0x33FC bytes) in the same data segment, so a write past the floor image would change it; no such write has been identified, and the trigger is unknown.

RPT-FILES-0001.note: Both Create Characters and Quickstart load the default save (R037+0x4184), which opens SAVES\DEFAULT without testing whether the open succeeded and then copies its roster into charactr.tmp through that handle, using a record count read from it.

RPT-LOAD-0001.note: Alt-L asks "Loading is irreversable. Proceed?" and then clears the party slots and frees the events before the load screen opens; in a game that screen has no Return button, and leaving it with Esc goes on with the emptied game (R037+0x8B76). Registered as B-14d327, with the fix flag FixLoadScreenEscape.

RPT-PLATFORM-0001.note: A disk-controller compatibility failure during film playback under DOS. The game's /Q switch (no opening, ending or death animation) is ported in StartUp.cs; film streaming is a host matter in the restoration (D-efcb07).

Printed map says “Freiberg im Breisgau”.note: An artwork/manual matter. The game's own data uses the same spelling: the DARKLAND.CTY record for the Breisgau city is named "Freiberg" with the long name "Freiberg-im-Breisgau" (its ruler is the "Count of Freiburg"), and DARKLAND.LOC has two places named Freiberg. Not a code defect.

Manual describes a Hall of Fame that is.note: The EXE contains a Hall of Fame routine (R038+0x26BE..0x2AB4: show DARKLAND.FAM, 5 records, and merge the party's fame), and DARKLAND.FAM ships with the game, but nothing calls it; the restoration's coverage lists these routines as unreferenced. The manual describes a feature the game never shows.

Battlefield saving is restricted to part.note: A deliberate rule: Save Game is offered in a battle only on a battlefield that persists, not in the keep, and outside real combat (a flag set by R014+0x0000).

Modern fullscreen, mouse, audio, or file.note: Fullscreen, mouse, audio and file-system problems of modern hosts (DOSBox, GOG builds) are platform matters unless traced to original game logic.

A purchased formula belongs to the purch.note: Formulas are known per character by design: the formula seller adds the bought formula to the member chosen in the pop-up (R064+0x31DC), while the alchemist's exchange teaches the leader (R066+0x13BC). The interface does not make the ownership obvious, but the code does what it was written to do.

The main-quest fortress monastery disapp.note: The fortress monastery's place record is changed by cards (for example R122+0x0000 turns it into an ordinary place once the demon is banished), but the path by which an attempt hides it and a later Sabbat brings it back has not been traced in the code.

Tarnhelm interaction causes the party to.note: A scripted card event described in the game's text, not a program crash; the item-quest crypt can also be purified with a saint or a potion as an intended route (CryptUnderTheRuinedChurch.cs, R108+0x084E, R108+0x0A5E).

Different Wild Hunts require different r.note: Intended: when the Wild Hunt quest is created (R087) its saint is drawn as rnd(0x88), any of the 136 saints, and its item at random; the Hunt card then offers that saint (R060+0x0978). A Hunt whose saint the party cannot get is the random draw, not a fault.

Protection prompts occur at every map ev.note: Tied to a third-party save editor. The game asks the protection question on entering the map only while event 0x63 has not been started, and then records that event for 0x3E80 hours (R030+0x0000); a save whose event list was altered, or left without a free slot, can bring the question back each time. The question itself is not asked in the restoration (D-f4c0e9).

RPT-INV-0001.note: A pack holds 64 stacks; adding a 65th stack that joins no existing stack is silently refused (R031+0x4A04). Buying (R032+0x0F60) charges the price before the add and taking an item from an inn store (R035+0x0A46) removes it from the store before the add, and neither screen tests for a full pack, so the item is lost. Loot moved into a full pack is already listed in the OriginalBehaviour remarks; transfers between members test for room first, and a save keeps all 64 entries, so the loss is at insertion, not in serialization.

RPT-INV-0002.note: A pack stack cannot pass 255: a join is made only when the total stays within 255, otherwise a new stack is started (R031+0x4A04). Two other counts are single bytes without that test: an inn store entry (already listed in the OriginalBehaviour remarks, see RPT-INN-0001) and the battle loot list, where a combatant who dies next to an existing pile has equal items added to the pile's entry in a byte (R014+0xE930), so a merged total above 255 wraps and the excess is lost.

RPT-INV-0003.note: No byte-sized aggregate of a character's or the party's items was found: the item counting routines sum into integers (R029+0x0C76) and a pack is at most 64 stacks of 255. The one overflow of an inventory-like table found in this check is the inn store's working table: a store with more than 100 different entries runs past it, and past 196 entries over memory that was not traced (D-674296). Whether that or anything else reaches the palette needs a runtime test in the original with stores of 100, 197 and 256 entries and the palette compared before and after.

RPT-INN-0001.note: Reproduced: an inn store entry's count is a byte, so the 256th item of one kind and quality turns it to 0 and the 257th to 1 (R035+0x10D2). Taking from an entry at 0 hands out an item and leaves 255 (R035+0x114A), so exactly 256 items can all be taken back, but from 257 on the multiples of 256 are lost. Documented in the OriginalBehaviour remarks, no register id.

RPT-INN-0002.note: The code has a mechanism by which inn storage in one long-running world breaks while a fresh world works: the store file only grows (a store emptied and given up stays in it), its header has room for a limited number of store offsets, and when a known store is written back the rewrite assumes a header under 128 bytes. Both defects are registered as divergences of the file layout (D-40780d, D-4277ec), so the restoration does not reproduce them. They do not explain the enemy cloth drops in the same report, and the link to that one case is not proven.

RPT-NUM-0001.note: Attributes and skills are kept in 1..99 and 0..99 by the routines that change them, so values above 99 arise only through an attribute maximum set without its limit (B-2ffc47) or outside the game. A temporary attribute boost (R029+0x4C04) is recorded in full but added through the 1..99 clamp and the cap of maximum plus largest boost (R029+0x0A72), while its expiry takes the full amount back (R029+0x448A): a boost cut on the way up, near 99 or on top of a larger boost already running, lowers the attribute for good (B-f134d1). Whole-party boosts are registered separately (B-8b2837, B-c14d7c, B-024865); single-member skill boosts are capped to 99 before recording and are symmetric.

RPT-WORLDMAP-0001.note: Not decided from the code in this check. The travel map's input and scrolling are ported from R030 with no registered defect of this kind. A test in the original under real DOS and under DOSBox with keyboard-only and mouse-only control would separate a game fault from host input (stuck keys, mouse at the screen edge).

RPT-COMBAT-0002.note: A registered original bug can produce it: when the battle loader drops an empty enemy group it also drops every group after it (B-a044f7), so if the first group on a level is empty the level has no enemies. The wilderness generator can write a group whose only kind has a count of 0 or below (R008+0x2ADC takes the second kind whatever its count), but whether a natural wilderness encounter produces such a first group was not shown. A test needs an encounter that yields that group.

RPT-MINE-0001.note: The report could not be tied to a card from the code: no card resource is named for a 'Mine Problem' and the mine cards with option menus ($MineP00/01 pit traps, the mine village, the mine levels) show no registered empty-screen path. The card involved and the step reached need to be identified in a run of the original.

RPT-INITI-0001.note: Card 0 ($Initi00, the developers' test card at R044+0x0000) is a normal entry of the card table. The only direct ways to it the restoration records are the developer stand-in card 5 (D-b8e305) and a previous-screen value of 0 (D-4d1f0e), both judged unreachable in play. Any transition to a card number held in a variable that is still 0 (a saved return card, for instance) would also open it; which one the reported case used needs a save from just before it appeared.

RPT-ROSTER-0001.note: In the original every character who joins at an inn gets the first figure of the figure list and the inn's starting colours, whatever the character's sex or occupation (R038+0x02F8); the figure and colours are then chosen with the Select Character Image and colour keys. A female or alchemist recruit therefore starts with a default figure that may not match. Whether the report describes more than this default (for example a change after saving and loading) needs a runtime check.

RPT-CALENDAR-0001.note: The code asks the copy-protection question whenever the protection event (kind 0x63) is not in the event log, and records it for 0x3E80 hours when answered (R030+0x0000; the inn records it for 0x2D0 hours). Repeated questions therefore point to that event being lost, which fits a loss of game state rather than a calendar fault, but the date rollback and the 'Jan 0' date were not explained from the code. A controlled start from April to August 1400 in the original, watching the event log and the date, would decide it.

RPT-REVOL-0001.note: Confirmed read: $Revol00 (R048+0x0000) uses option block 5 instead of 0 when the byte DS:5835 is not zero. The byte is 0 in the program's initial data and no instruction in the overlays writes it by address, so the restoration always uses block 0 (a comment at RevolutionHouseByDay.cs:23, no register entry). An indirect writer (a copy or string operation running over that address) has not been excluded, so whether block 5 is ever used in play remains open.

RPT-REVOL-0002.note: A question about earlier releases, which the 483.07 code cannot answer. In 483.07 the revolt house cards are ported, and specific branches that are never reached are registered one by one (for example the never-enabled options of the revolt houses); whether the whole family is reachable was not established here. An authenticated earlier executable with its MSGFILES is needed for a comparison.

RPT-PALETTE-0002.note: The save routine (R037+0x2ACE) writes the party size, the character count, the five slot ids, the figure codes (20 bytes) and the 0x78-byte colour block one after the other, then each character record, flushing before every record write; read as ported, it cannot place the colour block one word late while leaving the records in place, and the loader (R037+0x8ED4) reads the same fixed layout. The source of the displacement in the two saves is therefore not found in the save code; a byte comparison of saves around recruitment, dismissal, imprisonment and death in the original is still needed.

RPT-ALCH-0001.note: The formula seller (card 0x53, reached from alchemists' shops, universities and the abbot's clerk) offers formula (city number + 100/103/106/109) mod 22. Only formula records 0..21 (the potions 0x5F..0x66, all three grades) are ever for sale, and records 22..65 never are. The alchemists' formula exchange in R066 draws from all 66.

RPT-SAINT-0001.note: The saint table gives St.Paul (105) the function R039+0x7C6A. Its help (Strength and Endurance restored, half the Intelligence lost) and its feast day (day 66) are what DARKLAND.SNT describes for St.Paul the Simple. St.Paul the Simple (106) gets R039+0x7D0C, whose help repeats St.Thomas Aquinas's (R039+0x8B58). The help the text describes for St.Paul (Endurance, Charisma, Latin, Speak Common, Read/Write, a little Strength) is R039+0x9578, which no saint number reaches. Z-9318d7 records only that it is unreachable.

RPT-SAINT-0002.note: Each attribute blessing or potion records its own boost event, and nothing is replaced. A second boost while the first is in force records its points minus the excess over the maximum. But the attribute routine (R029+0x4E0C) caps the attribute at the maximum plus the largest single boost, so part of the recorded amount is never added. Both events later subtract what they recorded, which leaves the attribute below where it started. The mechanism is the same as RPT-EQUIP-0004, and one register entry covers both.

RPT-SAINT-0003.note: St.Theodore Tiro's help (R039+0x8A88) raises the skills of the equipped weapons (R029+0x0792), then raises Flail Weapons on its own. A member with a flail in hand therefore gets two Flail boosts (two events, both undone at expiry). DARKLAND.SNT describes him as raising Charisma, all weapon skills and Riding; the code gives no Riding and adds Endurance. St.Charity (R039+0x31FA) raises Flail only once.

RPT-EQUIP-0001.original: R031+0x43B2; R029+0x4D24; R029+0x448A; R039 charm saints (St.Polycarp and others)
RPT-EQUIP-0001.note: Deadly Blade, Strongedge and Great Power add to the member's weapon bonus byte (+0x34) and record a kind 0x4A event. When that event ends, the sheet's "Enhc/Bless" mark goes away.Hardarmor and Firewall (+0x41, +0x10) and the charm saints such as St.Polycarp record no event at all. Nothing in the game clears these bytes, which are saved with the member and read in every battle.

RPT-EQUIP-0002.note: There is no reapplication routine: each potion or saint writes the shared bytes directly. Other fields change only through carries and overwrites. Great Power and Strongedge add into the weapon byte and can carry into the damage nibble (noted in the OriginalBehaviour remarks). Hardarmor and St.Dunstan/St.Patrick add to the low nibble of +0x41, which can carry into the Firewall count. The charm saints overwrite the high nibble, and St.Polycarp overwrites the Firewall strength. The report's wording does not make clear which of these it means.

RPT-EQUIP-0003.note: Neither the potion code nor the hit code tests the weapon's kind: Great Power adds 14/22/30 to the member's weapon bonus byte (+0x34), and the hit routine (R014+0xAC08) applies that byte to every attack. The manual limits Great Power to impact weapons, flails and handguns (and Deadly Blade and Strongedge to certain kinds); the program never did, so this is a difference between the manual and the program rather than a defect of 483.07. B-23a975 covers the event type that Great Power records.

RPT-EQUIP-0004.note: The temporary boost (R029+0x4C04) reduces a second boost by the attribute's excess over its maximum and records the rest, as if the attribute could reach the maximum plus all boosts. The attribute routine caps it at the maximum plus the largest single boost (R029+0x4E0C). Example: with a maximum of 30, a +10 saint raises the attribute to 40; a +15 potion then records 5 but adds nothing; when both end, the attribute falls to 25. Saints and potions use the same routine, so this happens in either order.

RPT-RELIC-0001.note: Room 14 of the Templar fortress puts three different random items from 0x96..0xAB (the relics, including the relic weapons) into its loot groups. Each is written with quality 35 (0x23) and type byte 0x9F, not with the item's own quality (50..85 for the relic weapons) or its type from DARKLAND.LST.

RPT-RELIC-0002.note: The prayer chance depends only on the praying member's Virtue, the Divine Favor offered and the saint's own constants. R039+0x1FA0 takes a bonus argument, but all 136 saint functions pass 0. Neither the prayer screen nor the chance routines look at items, so carrying a relic does not change any prayer. Only the documentation suggests otherwise, so this is recorded as a difference between the manual and the program.

RPT-EVENT-0001.note: The sabbat's date and site come from a started fact (tag 1, type 4). When none exists, the date query returns day 0 of the year, printed as January 0, and the site query returns -1. The original then reads locations[-1] for the place (D-09b57b); the restoration prints nothing there. The fact is created when the sabbat quest starts (new game or the monthly check) and is renewed each time a sabbat begins, so the code does not show what removes it in play.

RPT-EVENT-0002.note: An event created to last 'forever' (9999 hours) is given the fixed end 23:00 on 31 December 1499 (R029+0x2C4E), and the expiry pass (R029+0x3F30) ends it on 1 January 1500. The witches' sabbat quest (R039+0x1B0C) is such an event: when it ends, its facts are cleared, including the planned next sabbat. A sabbat quest started after that date already has an end in the past and expires at the next expiry pass, so no further sabbats are planned. The same limit applies to every other 'forever' event.

RPT-CHURCH-0001.note: Confession takes standing / -10 + 11 hours in good standing (R057+0x03CC, signed division). This gives 1 hour at standing 100..109, 0 hours at 110..119, and a negative count from 120 upward. The time routine (R029+0x54D8) adds the count to the hour without borrowing, so the clock goes back and the hour can become negative. Standing above 99 is possible because a quest's resolution adds its value without a limit (R029+0x3E06). The thresholds in the code are 110 and 120, not the reported 130.

RPT-CHURCH-0002.note: Tithing first serves the 'member' whose number is the party's best Religion value (B-f30456), and this counts as one of the party-size visits. Normally that value is above the last member number. The loop then wraps to member 0 and visits only members 0 to n-2, so the last member gets no Divine Favor; in a party of one, nobody does. The register entry covers the cause.

RPT-BALANCE-0001.note: The church takes a tenth of the money. When that gift is over 600 pfennigs (so a purse of at least 6,010 pf), every member's Virtue rises by a thirtieth of his Religion (R057+0x067C). Religion 30 gives +1, and below 30 gives nothing. No event or cool-down limits repeats, so the gain is as repeatable as the code intends. The 16-bit purse quirks (B-42f89c and the signed low word of the tenth) are separate.

RPT-COMBAT-0001.note: Choosing Flee (R016+0x156E) sets the member's flee bit at once. When order mode ends with no spot chosen (R014+0xBCA8), the member keeps its current action and target. If the cursor still names the old target, the default (hand) weapon is readied while the action stays a missile action. A member with the flee bit set is skipped by the automatic engage and fight-back passes (R014+0xFADC, R014+0xFC50), and only arriving at a destination clears the bit. This could explain a shooter that keeps firing, with the melee weapon readied, but the repeated release itself has not been traced. A runtime test in 483.07 is needed: pause while aiming a bow, choose Flee, resume without clicking a spot, and watch the action word, the readied weapon and the reload timer.

RPT-MERCHANT-0001.note: By day the bowyers' guild opens its shop (shop 5) with the missile-weapon categories 0x30 / 0x83C (R065+0x0F18). Woken at night, it opens the same shop with 0xFF / 0x400 (R065+0x21BC), the mask the blacksmiths', swordsmiths' and armorers' cards use. So at night the bowyers offer hand weapons and other smith goods instead of their own. The other guilds use the same mask by day and by night.

RPT-ARMOR-0001.note: Equipped armour is held as a type and quality only. When the armour-eating cloud (kind 4, R019+0x0300) wears it down, R019+0x0968 lowers the quality of the first pack stack with that type and quality. Identical pieces share one stack (R031+0x4A04 joins equal code, type and quality), so every spare copy in that stack is worn down with the one being worn.

RPT-QUEST-0001.note: The fortress offers audiences and service only in a city without a town hall (location query 0x18 = 0, R050+0x1CEE). Its commission is recorded under the same owner (0x0A) as the town hall's. Only the town hall card (R054+0x1D08) looks for a resolved commission and pays it (city size x 7 groschen). The fortress card has no such check, and a city without a town hall hides that option on the square. So a fortress commission is never paid in money. The standing and reward written when the quest resolves (R029+0x3E06) still apply. The reward card (R080+0x038C) even has a case for the fortress card (0x1B) that is never reached.

RPT-QUEST-0002.note: When the clerk (or the fortress gate) says to come back, the card shuts the place to the party (event 0x3A) until 18:00 (or 05:00). The event names expiry handler 4, which would make a 24-hour 'welcome' event (0x3B) and raise the admission chance to 99. But the event is created with flag 0, and the expiry pass (R029+0x3F30) runs a handler only when flag bit 0 is set. So the appointment leaves no follow-up state: the next visit rolls as before. No card creates 0x3B, so the 'welcome' branch of the admission chance is never reached. This concerns the game itself, not the third-party viewer mentioned in the report.

RPT-WILDHUNT-0001.note: The Hunt's banishing saint is drawn from all 136 saints (0..135, R039+0x1F00), and only a party that knows it gets the banishing option. Monastery libraries draw their four saints from 0..134 with a generator seeded by the party and the place (R058+0x0928). Saint 135 is therefore never offered there, and each world's library saints are fixed. Other sources are a city's patron saint, the hermit by the fire (any of 0..135, at random) and a city lord's reward. Whether a given world can leave the drawn saint unobtainable depends on that world's data. Enumerating patron saints and library draws for a seed, against the drawn saint, would decide it.

RPT-STONE-0001.note: Each university offers a fixed stone level, ((location query 0x21 + 7) & 15) + 14, so 14..29 (R056+0x088C). A successful search upgrades the stone only when the party's stone is below that level (R056+0x0E7C). Otherwise it shows text 7, the same text as a failed search, but takes no money and no standing and opens no week-long closure. The success roll works as written; the missing 'your stone is already as good' message is a presentation matter.

RPT-POTION-0001.note: New-wind (0x70) calls the timed attribute boost (R029+0x4C04) for Endurance. It adds 6..11, 8..13 or 10..15 points by quality band (5 above quality 45), and an event takes them back after about a day. This is the potion's coded effect, written the same way as Ironarm and Quickmove. The mismatch is with the description, which promises restored Endurance.

RPT-POTION-0002.note: Black Cloud (0x61) cannot be drunk, and the combat Throw list leaves it out on purpose (R019+0x0C80 skips code 0x61). Its cloud (kind 2) has no case in the cloud's effect on combatants (R019+0x0300), so it changes no attribute or skill. Card scripts use it as an event item. The code does this deliberately; the mismatch is with the description.

RPT-POTION-0003.note: The Sunburst flash (marker type 6, R019+0x058A) acts on every able opponent of the thrower on the same floor that is not immune. It holds those whose facing is within two steps of the direction to the flash, and also the aimed-at target. It tests no distance and no line of sight: the Inside() test is applied only to the Thunderbolt and Arabian Fire blasts. The code works as written; the report describes the coded rule, not a fault in it.

RPT-POTION-0004.note: Great Power adds 14, 22 or 30 to the whole weapon-bonus byte, so its value carries across both nibbles. It records its bonus event under the pack index instead of the potion (B-23a975), and potion weapon bonuses are never undone when the event expires. So the effect has no real expiry, and drinking it again adds again without limit. The never-undone and unlimited-add parts are documented in OriginalBehaviour remarks, with no register id.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0035.note: The size lookup in TACANIM.DB ignores the result of the read, so for a family missing from the file it keeps the last record read. The restoration records this as a known original bug and, as a deliberate fix, uses the animation header's sizes for a missing family (D-e758be).

DL-ORIG-GAME-0034.note: When a chest is filled, the routine swaps entries of a 16-entry table but then picks the item by the raw roll, so the table has no effect and the same item can be chosen more than once (up to four stacks). Recorded as dormant code (Z-d0f3c7).

DL-ORIG-GAME-0033.note: For a corridor, the castle generator picks the cell for a wall decoration as the far end plus a roll (x = last column + roll - 1, or y = last row + roll - 1), not the near end plus a roll. Only a roll of 1 lands on the corridor itself; other rolls test, and may mark, cells beyond it.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0032.note: The view test does reject a nonpositive width or height only after clipping a negative origin, but its only caller passes the sprite box grown by 8 pixels each way, so width and height are always at least 8. The zero-extent case does not arise in the game.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0031.note: At the city gate the card reads the party's standing and the potion/saint availability once, on entry. After a fight that leaves the party at the gate (results 2 and 3), the menu is offered again with those entry values, and a second fight sets the standing to the entry value minus 40 again instead of lowering it further.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0030.note: Byte +0x1D of an enemy group record is never set when groups are cleared and keeps whatever the buffer held; the restoration notes this and uses 0. No reader of the byte in later combat has been identified, so whether the retained value has any effect is not decided by the code.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0029.note: Queued endurance and strength damage are signed bytes: a queue of 128 or more wraps negative, escapes the cap of 42 and is then subtracted as a negative amount. The restoration keeps the byte arithmetic; whether ordinary combat ever queues that much before it is applied has not been established.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0028.note: Withdrawn by its own author: the supposed mismatch came from reading the wrong message resource. The convent card in question shows its own text coherently.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0012.note: The inn-at-night card has a tenth option (show the first text, no time passes, go to the city outskirts card) that is never enabled and has no text line. Recorded as dormant (Z-1e0c6c).

DL-ORIG-GAME-0008.note: The card at R061+0x2278 (card 0x47) is the $Hanse00 card itself: it loads $Hanse00, and its rows and texts come from that file. $Hanse01 belongs to a separate, unfinished placeholder card (0x48, R062+0x0000). No card shows one file's name while using another's text.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0005.note: Soldier's Road (the Arms Outfitter) is the first row of $MILCR00 and has a complete action, but the card never enables it. Recorded as dormant (Z-44c195).

DL-ORIG-GAME-0006.note: Row 4 of $BLACK01 ('guard the guild block from saboteurs') is never offered and its action does nothing; rows 5 to 8 are likewise closed. Recorded as dormant (Z-44f5f6).

DL-ORIG-GAME-0007.note: Rows 6 and 7 of $COUNC00 (whose text is just '6' and '7') are never enabled; both actions show the first text, pass no time and go to card 4. Recorded as dormant (Z-21ab87, Z-9f11da, Z-0880d0).

DL-ORIG-GAME-0004.note: The council hall's weapons-training row is never enabled, although its chance and action are complete (five training events, a price named, or a standing loss when refused). Recorded as dormant (Z-a901ed, Z-67029d, Z-622af1). The price the hidden action names is computed from the city, while the five training events carry fixed fees of 50 and 25.

DL-ORIG-UI-0001.note: In the merchant screen Ctrl+F1..F5 changes the party leader and redraws only the party panel, then falls through into the Purchase/Sell list switch; prices on screen are not recomputed. Documented in OriginalBehaviour remarks and at BarterScreen.cs:370, no register id.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0001.note: Buying from a merchant takes the money first and then adds the item. If the member's pack already holds 64 stacks and none can take the item, nothing is added and the money is not returned.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0002.note: At the inn's stables the card shows text 1 when every present member is able and owns a mount, and text 7 otherwise. Only text 7 adds that the stablemaster asks whether any of the party's mounts are for sale, so the question appears when the party may have no mounts at all and is left out when everyone has one. The trading screen that follows is the same in both cases.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0003.note: In the news of affairs elsewhere, the 'nothing of interest' text (3) is shown in a city when neither the robber-knight nor the mine quest runs, but outside a city only while the mine quest runs: the wilderness branch tests the mine quest without the negation. The restoration reproduces and comments this (AffairsElsewhere.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0009.note: The robber-knight offer card ($Raubi00, card 0x90) looks up its quest event and uses the slot without checking for 'not found'; the reward card (0x91) does the same. The restoration uses 0 instead of reading through the stray pointer (D-b167a7, D-b83f90).

DL-ORIG-GAME-0011.note: With local standing of 50 or more and a full party (five members), asking the Schulz for help shows text 6 (he drops a florin into your hand) but adds no money. The same text after the low-standing fame roll does add one florin.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0010.note: When a village Schulz gave the robber-knight task, the reward card always shows text 1 ("he departs from your party"), and for the Hanse patron a coin flip shows text 6 ("your friend leaves you") or text 7. Neither choice looks at whether the guide was taken along (he joins only if accepted and the party has room), and the card removes nobody; the guide leaves only when his 90-day or 360-day term runs out.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0013.note: The night docks use the icy-water text and disallow swimming when the zero-based month is 10 or more or 4 or less (November to May). This is an explicit seasonal rule in the code, reproduced as is; it is a design choice about the season, not a code defect.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0014.note: The business-district card (0x14), reached from the night side street, loads its own $Busin00 texts by day and by night; only the picture differs. Its labels and actions therefore match, and no $SIDES01 text is left over its menu.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0015.note: On the night side street, choosing the grove (row 7) and meeting trouble on the way sets the place to return to after the night encounter to the night grove (0x22) unconditionally, although the hour has already passed and may now be daytime. The ordinary arrival and the day side street choose the day or night grove by the clock.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0016.note: The standing change draws a random number below |b| - |a|, and the random helper treats a range below 2 as 2. So a change with equal bounds, such as (-1, -1) for camping in the grove overnight, (-5, -5) or (4, 4), moves the standing by |a| or |a|+1, not by exactly |a|; a range of width 1, such as (1, 2), behaves the same. The restoration reproduces the arithmetic (documented on the random helper in MscRandom.cs); the rule works as written, so it is kept as a rule of the game, not a bug.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0017.note: Rows 2 to 7 of $OTHER00 (the literal placeholders 2 to 7) are never offered; their handlers would end the game (card 0x62). Recorded as dormant.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0018.note: The random-name draw uses counts 108, 88, 146 and 16 for its four name tables, but each table in the EXE holds more entries than that: two more first names (Wiprecht, Wolfgang), two more women's names (Suzanne, Viktoria), one more surname (of Zähringen) and one more merchant family (Welser). These trailing names can never be drawn. The restoration reads the same counts but does not record the unused entries.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0019.note: The never-enabled rows of the revolt house are recorded as dormant: by day row 5 (storm the house) and rows 6 to 8, at night rows 5 to 8. The rest of the revolt family is not unpublished: all nineteen resources $Revol00 to $Revol18 are used by cards in the restoration.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0020.note: Gathering gossip at the second faction's house shows texts 2 and 12, then text 2 again with text 3 or 4, because the original has no else between the two blocks.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0021.note: The second query is the compiled form of one condition, (fact == -1 and first house) or (fact == 1 and second house): it reads the same city fact again and changes nothing, so there is no behaviour difference. The restoration reads the fact once with the same result.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0022.note: Asking the altar boy in hour bands 4 and 5 (and above 7) names a stale stack word as the hour in the original; the restoration names the no-Mass hour and records this as uncertain. The night church is normally entered only at night, so these bands are hardly reached.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0023.note: Day Mass gives each member Religion/8 + Latin/35 + 1 Divine Favor, night Mass Religion/60 + Latin/40 + 1 (signed integer division, no absolute value or remainder). The two formulas are separate code in two separate cards and are reproduced as is; nothing shows that either is a mistake.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0024.note: Asking the captain of the guard passes a random 0 to 2 hours. Zero-hour actions are common in the card scripts (many options pass 0 hours), so a reply that takes no time is within the design; the restoration reproduces it.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0026.note: The 120-hour arm of the ban set after an extreme surrender is unreachable, since only a party at -75 or worse gets there; recorded as dormant.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0027.note: $SANCT00 holds texts that the sanctuary card never shows: text 4 (a second sanctuary menu), texts 5 to 8 (the priest's growing pressure to leave, ending in a forced departure with its own menu) and text 12 (a failed escape that ends in capture). The card shows only texts 0 to 3 and 9 to 11, and it is the only user of $SANCT00.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0036.note: In the segment-against-box clip test, when neither the bottom nor the top edge applies, the original uses an uninitialised intersection point (whatever the stack holds). The restoration keeps the previous clip point instead and records this as a divergence.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0037.note: The restoration's port of the missed-missile extension (R018+0x02BE) adds the last halved step after the final clear test, so an arrow could come to rest a few units past a wall; the port keeps this and names it in a source remark. The loop has not yet been traced in the original itself, so the finding stays open until it is.

DL-ORIG-GAME-0025.note: Retracted. A roll at or under the party's lowest Stealth plus Streetwise (10 to 99) gives text 10, the escape through the graveyard to the side street; a higher roll gives text 9, the stumble and retreat into the church after one hour. The card texts match their outcomes.
